## Natural history notes

A small darkling beetle characterized by its elongated oval body, dark brown to black coloration, and noticeably pale legs that give it the “pale-legged” appearance. In Florida, it is found in warm wooded or semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, forest edges, parks, yards, and areas with leaf litter, dead wood, bark, or decaying plant material. Adults are mostly ground- or vegetation-associated scavengers, while the larvae likely develop in decaying wood, fungi, leaf litter, or other organic material, helping recycle nutrients and serving as prey for spiders, birds, lizards, and other insect-eating animals.
